target_name: Cushion Large Relative to Operating Scale
rationale: The second leg, net liquid assets over revenue, is a near-mechanical duplicate of the already-tested "Cushion Runway Against Operating Cost Base" leg (revt − pi is simply revenue times one minus the margin, so the cross-sectional ranks will be almost perfectly correlated), making this a cosmetic re-specification rather than a new economic conditioner.

target_name: Cheap Book Value in Asset-Heavy Firms
rationale: This is a legitimate and clearly framed ablation of whether the price-below-liquid-assets comparison is essential, but the archive already contains two close cousins (B/M gated by cushion-to-book and revenue-cheapness gated by cushion-to-assets, both with ~zero alpha) that largely pre-answer the question, so its expected informational yield is modest.

Questioning the realizability of the reported current assets via current-asset growth outrunning sales growth is the first genuinely new economic mechanism in this batch and is well matched to the stated hypothesis, though the reviewer should note it partially overlaps the published working-capital-accrual and inventory-growth anomalies and that an unwinsorized growth difference will be rank-dominated by tiny-revenue firms.

Testing the symmetric low-enforceable-debt case on the earnings side is a coherent and untested complement to the two negative-signed earnings-yield gates in the archive, but it is close to the well-documented result that value/earnings-yield strategies work best among low-leverage firms, so novelty is limited and the second leg is identical to the one already used in generation 5.

target_name: Volatile Levered Stub Funding Itself by Dilution
rationale: This is literally the union of two already-evaluated signals — the levered-stub-with-volatile-earnings gate and the levered-diluter gate — with their second legs merged by SUMRANK, which is an ensemble of tested components rather than a substantively new claim, and each ingredient (distress, share issuance, earnings volatility) is an independently published anomaly.

Liability growth is economically distinct from the cushion-change and share-issuance conditioners already tried and provides a clean contrast with the asset-side inflation story, but it is effectively the published net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly used as a gate, and the archive pattern shows most such MIN gates merely dilute the base cushion-to-price leg's 5.9% alpha.
